diagnosis.root_cause: The router has never produced a heartbeat record. This indicates missing router monitoring or management reachability, although subscriber service is currently operational.
evidence: The router heartbeat status is 'never' with no last_checkin, meaning no heartbeat record has ever been collected.
The subscriber ONU is online and responding, with normal RX power of -21.9 dBm and TX power of 2.34 dBm.
The seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains in the normal band, TX and bias current are healthy, and distance is constant at 87.
All probed peers on EPON0/4 are online, ruling out an ONU, splitter, or PON-port outage.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and subtree queries and has healthy CPU, memory, and temperature, ruling out an OLT failure.
Authentication is consistent, sessions are within the normal baseline, VLAN 1124 is correctly provisioned, and traffic is passing.
Therefore the only abnormal condition is the absence of router heartbeat data, with no evidence of an EPON or subscriber-service failure.

remediation.action: Verify that router monitoring and heartbeat collection are enabled, confirm management-plane reachability and credentials, and check whether the router is configured to report to the monitoring system. Do not dispatch for an access-network outage unless heartbeat failure is confirmed as an actual router outage.

ground_truth.root_cause: The router has no check-in record of any kind, which means it was never enrolled in heartbeat monitoring rather than that it stopped responding. Its customers are authenticated, holding long sessions and passing normal traffic.
expected_reasoning: The router's heartbeat status is 'never' with a null last_checkin
That is different from a heartbeat that went stale, which would carry a timestamp and an elapsed time
No record at all indicates the router was never enrolled in the check-in mechanism
The ONU behind it is online with RX -21.9 and TX 2.3, both normal
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are all responding normally
Sessions are active with a 683 minute mean, close to the 11.9 hour network norm
Daily traffic is steady across all seven days with no interruption
Customers on this router are being served, so there is no outage
The finding is a monitoring gap, not a network fault

expected_escalation.review_reason: Router is not enrolled in heartbeat monitoring and should be added

distractors: A null heartbeat looks worse than a stale one and invites a Disaster conclusion
A scheduled scan targeting the router frames it as the suspect
The correct answer is that nothing is wrong with the network
